status: Bundled and enabled; local portable candidate built and verified without launching/installing it. Overall performance victory over VLC remains unproven.
change: Compatible 8-bit SDR NV12 filtering retains the existing separable LUT weights and bilinear chroma, skips full-sized RGB intermediates, and retires stale scaling targets on re-entry. No lower-precision framebuffer policy. Unsupported/specialized settings retain the original path.

nativeFunctional.scope: Hidden correctness, balanced filtering, timing disabled/cache4/direct=yes. Includes hardware and libdav1d AV1, controls, geometry/reconfigure, audio and localhost playback. Does not establish visible presentation cadence.

frameCases.scope: 28 isolated frame runs. Actual path proved by redraw descriptions, exact 2s position, decoder verified, detailed nonblank picture, paired pixels. Thirteen cases enforce pixel bounds; adaptive HDR verifies fallback and reports pixels without a strict bound.

appUnit.scope: Desktop PlaybackSession geometry explicitly deferred; never counted as passed.

validation.package: 10 runtime files; Read-AperturePackage cryptographic verification passed. Not installed or launched.

gpuPassDiagnostic.scope: Offscreen renderer-reported pass timing diagnostic: sum of average redraw-pass times for a fixed 2s frame, three rotated rounds, same DLL with direct filtering off/on. GPU profiling is enabled here and disabled in normal Aperture. This does not establish visible playback throughput, app CPU/RAM or shader-arithmetic cost. No VLC run.
limits: The baseline first separable pass dominates the reported ~4ms. These timer-bracketed backend calls can include submission/query effects; the cause of that large interval is not established.
The diagnostic cannot be translated into a percentage app performance improvement.
Whole-player performance after adopting this build remains unmeasured because visible tests are deferred.

performanceEvidence: Prior isolated native screen saved about30MiB with the direct prototype; see docs/evidence/balanced-memory-20261018/research/direct-nv12-experiment/h264-screen-v3/results.json. This is historical engine evidence, not a new measurement of this bundled app. Prior balanced full-player CPU results remain in docs/evidence/balanced-frame-resources-20261018/review.json. Saved VLC data retains its original date/session.
limits: No new visible full-app CPU/RAM/throughput comparison was run after this adoption. No VLC process was launched.
Hidden output checks and paused diagnostic pass timing cannot prove the whole-player ranking. GPU profiling is enabled only for that diagnostic and disabled normally.
